subject.title: feat(agents): configured agent env reaches spawned subprocesses

question: Should OpenClaw accept broad literal `agents.list[].env` for CLI, exec, ACP/ACPX, and stdio MCP child processes, or prefer the narrower exec-only SecretRef direction represented by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96309?
rationale: The patch changes public config, credential handling, subprocess inheritance, and session reuse semantics across several runtime owners, so automation cannot choose the permanent security boundary.

options.title: Choose the canonical env contract first
options.body: Resolve broad literal per-agent env versus narrower SecretRef/exec-only env, then require this PR or the alternative to match that decision before merge.

options.title: Accept this broad env contract
options.body: Treat this PR as the canonical sanitized child-process env surface once failing checks are refreshed and green.

options.title: Pause behind exec-only SecretRef
options.body: Keep this PR paused, or close it later, if the narrower SecretRef path becomes the accepted and merged implementation.

recommendation.title: Choose the canonical env contract first
recommendation.body: Resolve broad literal per-agent env versus narrower SecretRef/exec-only env, then require this PR or the alternative to match that decision before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the clearest available review and code-history signal across config, exec, and ACPX runtime boundaries.
